last_transition_reason: The proof gives the standard and correct formal-power-series expansion of the product, justifies coefficient extraction for a fixed j by showing only finitely many tuples can contribute, and then identifies the contributing tuples with finite multisets of I. This yields exactly the claimed signed enumeration over X_j. It matches the lemma sketch and role in the assembly, and it does not rely on any undeclared or forbidden dependency.
latest_nl_proof:
Let
F(q) := product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) = product_{s in I} ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)).
We interpret [q^j] in the formal power series ring Z[[q]]. This is legitimate because every s in I satisfies s >= a+1 >= 1.

For each s in I,
(1 - q^s)^(-1) = sum_{m>=0} q^(ms)
in Z[[q]], since multiplying the right-hand side by 1 - q^s gives 1. Hence
product_{s in I} (1 - q^s)^(-1) = product_{s in I} sum_{m_s>=0} q^(m_s s).
Because I is finite, expanding this finite product gives
product_{s in I} (1 - q^s)^(-1) = sum_{(m_s)_{s in I}} q^(sum_{s in I} m_s s),
where the sum runs over all tuples of nonnegative integers (m_s) indexed by I.

Likewise,
product_{s in I} (1 - q^(r+s))
= sum_{S subseteq I} product_{s in S} (-q^(r+s))
= sum_{S subseteq I} (-1)^{|S|} q^(sum_{s in S} (r+s)).

Multiplying the two expansions, we obtain in Z[[q]]
F(q) = sum_{S subseteq I} sum_{(m_s)_{s in I}} (-1)^{|S|} q^( sum_{s in S}(r+s) + sum_{s in I} m_s s ).

Now fix j >= 0. Only finitely many terms on the right can contribute to the coefficient of q^j: the set I is finite, and if sum_{s in I} m_s s <= j then for each s in I we have 0 <= m_s <= j/s. Therefore we may read off the coefficient term-by-term:
[q^j] F(q) = sum_{S subseteq I} (-1)^{|S|} * #{ (m_s)_{s in I} : sum_{s in I} m_s s + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j }.

For each fixed S, such tuples (m_s) are in bijection with finite multisets lambda of elements of I: m_s is the multiplicity of s in lambda. Under this bijection,
wt(lambda) = sum_{s in I} m_s s.
Therefore
#{ (m_s)_{s in I} : sum_{s in I} m_s s + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j }
= #{ lambda : wt(lambda) + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j }.
Substituting this into the previous formula gives
[q^j] F(q) = sum_{S subseteq I} sum_{lambda : wt(lambda) + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j} (-1)^{|S|}.
But by definition, the pairs (S, lambda) appearing in this double sum are exactly the elements of X_j. Hence
[q^j] product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) = sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^{|S|},
as required.
role_in_parent: Provides the direct combinatorial interpretation of the same coefficient that L2 identifies algebraically.
statement_nl:
Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and j >= 0. Set I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. Define X_j to be the set of all pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, and wt(lambda) + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j, where wt(lambda) denotes the sum of the elements of lambda. Then
[q^j] product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) = sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^{|S|},
where |S| is the cardinality of S.

domain_restrictions: a and b are integers with 0 <= a <= b.
r and j are nonnegative integers.
I is the finite set of integers from a+1 through b.
The index s ranges over I in the product and in the sum over S.
S is any subset of I.
lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, with repetition allowed through multiplicity.
wt(lambda) is the sum of the multiset elements counted with multiplicity.
The condition wt(lambda) plus the sum over s in S of (r+s) equals j is exact, not approximate.
The product is finite, and if a equals b then it is an empty product.
q is treated as a formal power series variable rather than a numerical parameter.
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every choice of integers a, b, r, j with 0 <= a <= b and r, j nonnegative, if I is the set of integers from a+1 through b and X_j is the set of all pairs (S, lambda) where S is a subset of I and lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I satisfying wt(lambda) plus the sum over s in S of (r+s) equals j, then the coefficient of q^j in the finite product over s in I of (1 - q^(r+s)) divided by (1 - q^s) is equal to the sum over all pairs in X_j of (-1) to the size of S.
quantifier_order: For all integers a, b, r, j satisfying 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and j >= 0.
Define I from a and b as the set of integers from a+1 through b.
Define X_j from a, b, r, j as the set of all pairs (S, lambda) with S a subset of I and lambda a finite multiset of elements of I such that wt(lambda) plus the sum over s in S of (r+s) equals j.
Then the coefficient of q^j in the finite product over s in I of (1 - q^(r+s)) divided by (1 - q^s) equals the signed sum over X_j.

witness_dependencies: Each admissible witness pair (S, lambda) is constrained by the fixed parameters a, b, r, and j through the set I and the equality wt(lambda) plus sum over s in S of (r+s) equals j.
There is no separate existential witness in the final identity beyond choosing a pair (S, lambda) from X_j.
The sign of each contribution depends only on the size of S, not on lambda.
